punchline: Seneca's answer to "life is too short" was that we waste much of it, and he asked how few days actually went as intended.
thirty_sec: People complain that life is short. Seneca, writing to Paulinus, says life is long enough if it is well invested, and compares it to wealth: modest riches under a careful guardian grow, vast ones under a bad owner scatter. Then he asks the reader to go over their own days and count how few turned out as intended, and concludes you are dying before your time.
